hf-frame: Formalism.HC.Frame. The group A is Fin n with a chosen additive group structure (Idx ord); the numbering of A in the text is this identification with Fin n, and Frame.ofNat v is the element numbered v mod n. h is h0 and a0 is gen0; injectivity of h on A0 is the field zsmul_generator_eq_zero_of_projection. The Galois group GG is (ℤˣ × ℤˣ) × Multiplicative A; ι, ι_d, Ψ, τ1, τ2 are cc, iod, Psi, tau1, tau2, and θ_q is psC. X^± are Frame.Xp and Frame.Xm (TrivialOnFirstFactor means trivial on tau1 of A0). The index o is ord / n0, which equals [A : A0] (index_A0_eq_o).
hf-host-field-of-character: UpperTheory.Top.IsChiField. The Lean quantifies over natural numbers a with τ ζ = ζ^a and uses jacobiSym a q, jacobiSym a d and ψ.val a. The description as a compositum is a consequence added for orientation; it is not part of the Lean definition.
hf-framed-host-field: Formalism.HC.HostRaw. The isomorphism γ is gal : (E ≃ₐ[ℚ] E) ≃* GG, so γ⁻¹(art u) is gal.symm (art u); j is cycEmb and the condition (iii) is art_spec. Condition (iv) is art_neg_one, art_h, art_d and art_q. HostAx bundles HostRaw with the derived structure HostDer, which holds for every HostRaw (HostRaw.der), so the two carry the same data. χ_θ is HostRaw.prim θ, and 'χ is a character of E' is HostRaw.IsCharE.
hf-host-field-properties: HostRaw.der proves HostDer, a structure with about twenty-five fields. The proposition states the ones used in this chapter: art_surj, cm, finrank_E and finrank_F, art_ch, frob, inertia_d, unramEF and principal. The proofs given are the standard arguments; the Lean proves all fields through Der.hostCore and related lemmas.
hf-kernel-host-field: The hypothesis is UpperTheory.Top.KerChi ψ H; the conclusion is IsChiField ψ φ.e H.q H.d H.E (UpperTheory.Top.isChiField).
hf-host-field-rows: HostParam.Seam.FieldRows H b, with fields psQ, sqq, QS_exact, QS_le, o_pow, q_ne_three, split_small and small_le. The same conditions appear as fields of Formalism.BasicNotions.Host, with b the field splitBound.
hf-host-field-exists: UpperTheory.Top.fieldChi. Condition (c) is KerChi, (d) is KeptInXp and ExceptionalCharacterKept for Level.cyc ψ (which has no exceptional character, so the second half says the primitive character of psC is not in its KEPT set), and (e) is TwistForm. The Lean states o = (Level.cyc ψ).o, which is the order of ψ. The proof follows the construction AnyGrp.frame and AnyGrp.host through ModData: Step 1 is UpperTheory.Top.ordAny (c is the least value of n(e) = |ξ(ker cl_e)|, which is antitone in e); Step 2 is EvenGrp.QS (the least natural number with the property, Nat.find) and dvd_QS; Steps 3 and 4 are ModData.frame, ModData.art (with w = D.w) and art_surj; Step 5 is CharData.toHostRaw and ModData.exists_sqq; Step 6 is the fields art_neg_one, art_h, art_d and art_q of ModData.charData; Step 7 is ModData.psQ, ModData.exact with AnyGrp.exact_data, AnyGrp.QS_le and conductor_divisor_bounds; Step 8 is kerChiAny; Step 9 is AnyGrp.keptInXp and exceptional_character_condition; Step 10 is twistAny, through exA and exSign. The Lean's e0 is max(e1, 2, 4N_ψ, 64|⟨ψ⟩|).
hf-admissible-pair: UpperTheory.Top.WinPair eps Y q d. The Lean definition puts no condition on ε and Y; the restriction to ε > 0 and Y > 1 only fixes the domain. The consequences in the last paragraph are UpperTheory.Top.pairHyp.
hf-good-pair: UpperTheory.Top.PairGood M eps Y X q d. The twisted function is tw ξ q d i j and the height of the zero box is height M eps Y j. The Lean quantifies over all primitive χ inducing the function; there is exactly one.
hf-zero-density-box: Formalism.HermitianLattices.Ext.PrimitiveCharacterCasts.ZeroDensityBox, proved by ZD.zero_density_box through a mollifier, zero detection and a duality (large sieve) inequality. It counts characters that have a zero, so it is weaker than the published estimates, which count zeros; the Lean proves it directly. This, and not Theorem hf-zero-density-regions, is the zero-density input of the choice of auxiliary primes (through QH.count_bad_core).
hf-zero-density-regions: GlobalTheory.ZerosNearOne.density_and_regions combines GlobalTheory.ZeroDensityMult.zero_density_mult for (a) with GlobalTheory.ZeroFreeHalf.main for (b) and (c). Part (a) is a special case of the log-free zero-density estimates (σ = 1 − 1/400, T = Q); (b) is the zero-free region with at most one exceptional zero, measured by log max(N, N|Im ρ|); (c) is de la Vallée Poussin's region. The plan placed this result under the choice of auxiliary primes, but it is not reachable from that choice: it enters the proof through Formalism.MainNotions.LitThin (GlobalTheory.ZerosNearOne.main), a hypothesis of GlobalTheory.Top.designExists_of_tuSize_aux4n_litThin in Chapter 13.
hf-mean-square: QH.meanSqK, with QH.MeanSq, QH.S, PPset m₀ a₀ U and the hypotheses QH.admitted ε Y U m₀ a₀. The proof follows the Lean: Step 2 is meansq_expand, Step 3 is jacobi_class and abs_pair_sum_eq (s(N') is soutPart m₀ N'), Step 4 is QH.twistK with A = 800K and B = K + 1 and meansq_split, Step 5 is pairs_one and pairs_r (s_N(p) is sP (cN y) N p and R_N(m₀) is RR (cN y) m₀ N), all packaged in QH.meanSq_abs, and Step 6 uses RR_le, exists_primePowerSum_le_mul_log, sPsq_le and sum_cN_le (Lemma hf-prime-power-sums). The text uses one constant C₁ for the four estimates of that lemma; the Lean has four constants and C = C3 + 25C1² + 4C2² + 20C1C2 + C4² with C2 = 3.
hf-chebyshev-from-twisted-sum: QH.box_of_S. Its conclusion QH.Box Q C τ Y (Y^K) χ also repeats the hypothesis QH.GoodC Q χ. The Lean takes q to be any natural number and (n/q) the Jacobi symbol; the text states the case of a prime q, which is the one used. Step 1 is QH.tailK (through tail_diff_schi for the first bracket, tail_contour for the second, and the numerical lemmas tailK_num and tail_num_third), Step 2 is finite_splitting_of_group with num_box, and Step 3 is QH.kappaC with tail_mertens. T_χ(z) is tailL χ z and Σ_χ is Formalism.ZeroFreeDirichlet.Schi.
hf-most-primes-good: QH.pair_share, stated here with X = Y^K; the Lean allows any X ≤ Y^K, which follows by restriction. 'Good at level Q' is QH.Box Q C τ Y (Y^K). P_1 is primePairSetFirst z and P_2(q) is primeSetTwoBounds z z' q, whose congruence condition is oddM z q ∣ d + 1 with oddM z q = q · ∏ of the odd primes up to z. The proof follows QH.stage1 and QH.stage2, both from QH.stage, which uses QH.count_bad (through zero_density_box), QH.meanSqK, QH.bad_share, QH.box_of_S and count_a (primes in progressions with the Siegel bound excBound).
hf-good-pairs-exist: QH.pairEx proves UpperTheory.Top.PairEx. The Lean proof uses QH.pair_exists (from pair_share with η = 1/2) and QH.kappa4, whose source QH.kappa4_loglog gives |L'/L(1,χ)| ≤ 1000 log log Q + C.
hf-bounded-characters: UpperTheory.Top.boundedTw, through boundedTw_key. The Lean assumes 0 < ε, 1 ≤ x and Y ≤ x; the good pair needs Y > 1 only through its definition here.
hf-windows: A scale is Formalism.BasicNotions.Scale (fields x, eps, J with 1 < x, 0 < eps < 1/52, 1 ≤ J); δ1, b and X' are Scale.delta1, Scale.b and Scale.X'. A set of scales is GlobalTheory.EX.Scales la with Scales.Mem. The window property of W is the property of Definition wl-windows (Formalism.HC.HasWindows), restated in Scales.windows; the text cites that definition.
hf-windows-exist: UpperTheory.Top.winPairs, whose Lean statement also takes UpperTheory.Top.PairEx as a hypothesis; that is Theorem hf-good-pairs-exist. The data (Y, q, d, e) form UpperTheory.Top.WinDatum. The hypothesis is UpperTheory.Top.VWinAt ψ 401. The bound in (c) is VVle E ⌊x^400⌋ (sqrt (exp (x^ε))), which quantifies over an algebraic closure of E and the local data at each prime used to define the lengths of Ш.
hf-behrend-set: Formalism.FrobeniusOrbits.hostThickExists proves HostThickExists with C = 32, from Mathlib's Behrend.sphere and Behrend.exists_large_sphere. Behrend's theorem excludes three-term progressions, the relation 2(s2 − s1) = s3 − s1. This statement excludes all relations with |i|, |j| ≤ L at the cost of the factor 1/L and the dependence on log L; it is a variant proved by the same construction, not a special case of the published theorem.
hf-behrend-set-at-scale: UpperTheory.BernoulliSumsFrobeniusOrbits.thickFrame2, where hE ε = 2 + 8ε. The Lean removes 0 from the set given by hostThickExists to obtain 4L|T| ≤ n0 (thickFrame2_card). Step 3 follows the Lean's use of the inequality of arithmetic and geometric means with δ = ε/(3C); Step 2 is the comparison of (n0/L)e^(−Cv) − 1 with (n0/L)e^(−2Cv), done in the Lean through thickFrame2_large.
hf-thick-orbits: Formalism.HC.Frame.hostThickOrbit, with T^♯ = Frame.InTranslate T u0 and the two parts thick_part_one (through thick_key) and thick_part_two. It is applied to Frobenius orbits of places in GlobalTheory.HTW.LongWindow.main (at most two thick places in a window of a long orbit) and in NoThreeConsecutiveThickPlaces.
hf-adapted-ranks: GlobalTheory.EX.RankVal s R. The correction term is TOv s * nWv R s with TOv s = ⌈x^377⌉ and nWv R s = 8⌈10 r (f + f²(k − 1)³ L²/m)/8⌉, L = x^ε. In the Lean, Ranks extends Frame, so a rank datum includes its Galois datum, with the numbering of its group; n is R.n = R.ord.
hf-host: Formalism.BasicNotions.Host R, which extends HostAx R.toFrame. Condition (a) is the fields flPS, sqq, QS_exact, QS_le, o_pow, q_ne_three, splitBound, split_small and small_le; (b) is qd_big; (c) is φ₀ ∈ cmType and 𝔟 with 𝔟_spec and 𝔟_stable; (d) is levelPrimes, g, pde, pde' and level_coprimeS; (e) is ccK; (f) is TT, T2, u0, Lw, second_set_range, second_set_no_relation and CT2. The primes p, p' are the fields pde, pde'.
hf-host-extension: HostParam.Seam.exists_host. Theorem hf-good-host-exists has in the Lean the hypothesis UpperTheory.Top.admitted R H0, which is this lemma for the given R and H0; UpperTheory.Top.admissible_ranks_of_CMDatum proves it for all R and H0.
hf-host-conditions: Formalism.HC.EAtH Λ H TT x ε C, with Λ a Formalism.HC.Level (a KSet with an integer o). Condition (c) is ExceptionalCharacterKept: if psK = some ψ then ψ is the primitive character of psC, and if psK = none then the primitive character of psC is not in KEPT. For the cyclic level, which has psK = none, the condition is not empty, contrary to the plan's paraphrase: it says that χ_{−q} is not the primitive character of a power of ψ. Condition (d) is Frame.Shares TT (x^(−1+ε)).
hf-good-host: GlobalTheory.EX.HostGood s C8 C5 c6 Cb H q0, the conjunction of HostVal, HostArith, secondSet_card_lower_bound, 4 Lw |T2| ≤ n0, QDq, BoxW, |dlogH| ≤ x^ε, ThinOK, BadOK, disjointness of BB r (g 0) and BB r (g 1), the norm elements π ≡ 1, pde ≡ pde' ≡ 1 mod lcm(15, N), the conditions on q0, and levelPrimes = {g0, g1, pde, pde', q0}. The items are regrouped here. 'Pair scale' is PairWin s Y ∧ PairRow Y ε H. The class splitK of a level prime is written as 'prime to N with (−d/ℓ) = 1'. Condition (g) is BadOK s Cb H, with B = baseOf s 0 0 H. Its primes are those p < ⌈X'⌉ with B.IsResidueClassZero p, that is H.cls p = inertClass, which by primeClass means p ∤ Q_S, p ≠ q, d, (−d/p) ≠ 1 and psAt p ≠ 1; for such p this is p ∤ N, (−d/p) = −1 and first sign −1. y_{p''} is hPH H p, the A-component of a Frobenius element chosen with Classical.epsilon; for p ∤ N it is the A-component of art(p) (Proposition hf-host-field-properties (c)). The orbit condition is Arith.Loc.Good B (hPH H p) (Arith.bsH (stepP B (hPH H p) p) t), and stepP is hPH H p because an inert-class prime is not of class signal. L_2 is B.Ltwo = 2 sSup {L1 p : p of inert class} with L1 p = ⌈log_p((k x^26)^4)⌉ (Scale.A = 26); the set is bounded, so the supremum is the largest value.
hf-norm-primes: UpperTheory.T3.levelData, applied with UpperTheory.T3.shortNorm (Theorem hf-norm-primes-short) and UpperTheory.T3.smallOne. The norm condition is GlobalTheory.Mem.An.NormOne d N g. Step 1 is UpperTheory.T3.normPrimesN, Step 2 is typePrimesN with exists_pair_disjoint and GlobalTheory.choice_count (Lemma hf-exceptional-primes), Step 3 is exists_three_primes_one_mod_le_rpow, Step 4 is mod_small. The Lean proves SmallOne (the least prime ≡ 1 mod M is at most M^A) from GlobalTheory.T.primesInProgressions_relativeError through smallOne_of; the text cites Linnik's theorem, which gives the same statement. The bound r ≤ x^5 is part of GlobalTheory.EX.rank_basic_bounds.
hf-host-chebyshev: QH.thinH proves UpperTheory.Top.ThinH with c = 1. Its hypothesis on real characters is UpperTheory.Top.RealBox. Step 1 is QH.small_zeros, Step 2 is QH.real_cond with level_dvd, and Steps 3 and 4 are QH.thin, which combines QH.psi_thin (Theorem hf-pnt-character), QH.g_integral (Lemma hf-chebyshev-integral) and QH.int_thin. The Lean's g_χ for a character of E is Formalism.HC.An.gChi, equal to QH.G0 by gauss_sum_function_eq.
hf-top-classes: UpperTheory.BernoulliSumsFrobeniusOrbits.topsChoiceH, through topsBase, topsFrame and topsGroup. Step 1 is lt_of_classC0' with the condition kron of PairRow, Step 2 is ltwo_le' and logb_le', Steps 3 to 5 are topsGroup with select (Lemma hf-random-selection), orbit_sum, not_good_le and orbit_terms (Lemma hf-orbit-failure), and Step 6 is tg_num and shares_of_counts. The random set is the product weight pw on subsets of A, with probabilities δ1 on A0 and 3δ1/4 off A0. The Lean uses C = max(C8, 2) in place of C8.
hf-good-host-exists: UpperTheory.Top.hostOfField, which is UpperTheory.T3.hostOfFieldOf applied to shortNorm and smallOne. The Lean statement has two further hypotheses: FieldRows H0 ⌊Y^(ε/5)⌋, which is the splitting bound here, and admitted R H0, which always holds (UpperTheory.Top.admissible_ranks_of_CMDatum) and is omitted. Its conclusion also records H.toHostAx = H0 and H.CT2 = CT2.
hf-hosts-on-windows-def: GlobalTheory.EX.HostExW la P, with P of type HostReq.
hf-hosts-on-windows: UpperTheory.Top.supplyChi : ∀ ψ, VWinAt ψ 401 → HostExW (3/2) (GChi ψ).req. The requirement GChi ψ is EAtH (Level.cyc ψ) H TT x ε 4 ∧ VVle H.E R.t (sqrt b), and sqrt b = exp(x^ε/2). The proof follows UpperTheory.T3.supplyOfAdmOf. Behrend's construction enters only through the thick set T2 of the host (Corollary hf-behrend-set-at-scale); the exponent e of the 2-power tower is chosen by the size condition x^(2+8ε) ≤ c 2^e ≤ 2x^(2+8ε) alone (UpperTheory.Top.exists_pageN), so the announcement's 'choice of the Iwasawa tower using Behrend' does not describe the Lean.
hf-good-orbit: A tiled set of positions is Formalism.G0.GoodOrbitIntervalTileCondition n' P L₂ K r u M₀ G' N₁, the conjunction of CondA (a), CondTiles (b, with Marked and cell) and CondIntervals (c), where window n i L is W(i, L). Formalism.MainNotions.G.IsGoodOrbit supplies the parameters: K = KG s, r = rG s, u = goodU δ1, M₀ = orbitSmallMultiplicity r h x, G' = goodG' r δ1 h x and N₁ = orbitWindowCount r δ1 h x, with h = hG s = 2 + 8ε; orbitSmallMultiplicity divides by 10^(−(6r+1)), which is the factor 10^(6r+1) here. The good orbit is Arith.Loc.Good B y b with b = Arith.bsH y t; bsH y t is the element ofNat v with the least v such that ofNat v + i·y = t for some natural number i, which is the element of the coset t + ⟨y⟩ with the least number. The positions are topsPos B y b.
hf-primes-progressions: Three statements proved in the Lean. (a) is Formalism.HermitianLattices.Ext.LogarithmicIntegralBounds.PNTAPRelW, proved by pnt_progressions_relative_weak_holds; piAP X M b counts primes p ≤ X with p ≡ b mod M, mainAP is m_M(b, X) (with the real part of χ1(b), which is χ1(b) for a real character), and liX is li. It is a consequence of Gallagher's prime number theorem, which holds for X ≥ M^C; the range log X ≥ C0 log M log(log M + 2) here is smaller. (b) is page_across, derived from the zero-free region Formalism.ZeroFreeDirichlet.ZFRDirichlet (zFRDirichlet) for the modulus M1M2 ≤ Z²; it is the Landau-Page theorem. (c) is Formalism.ZeroFreeDirichlet.ExcBound (excBound) with exponent 1; ExcBound itself is Siegel's form, β ≤ 1 − c(ε)M^(−ε) for every ε > 0, and only ε = 1 is used here (in count_a).
hf-twisted-prime-sums: QH.twistK. The bad integers are the set bad in its proof; the uniqueness uses page_across and jacobi_separate, the main estimate is twist_one (through twist_decomp and main_twist_bound, with liX_pow_le for li(U^β)), the lower bound |P| ≥ U^(9/10) is count_a, and the final numerical comparison is final_ineqK. The Lean's x and X are Y and U here.
hf-prime-power-sums: (a) is QH.exists_primePowerSum_le_mul_log (with C = 3), (b) is QH.sPsq_le, (c) is QH.RR_le and (d) is QH.sum_cN_le. s_N(p) is sP (cN y) N p and R_N(m₀) is RR (cN y) m₀ N. The Lean has a separate constant for each part; the text takes the largest.
hf-log-derivative-box: Formalism.HermitianLattices.Ext.BoxTail.tail_box_negLD, stated there for −L'/L (negLD). The proof uses Formalism.ZeroFreeDirichlet.landau_lemma_lfunction_zeros with lfunction_polynomial_growth and inverseBound, and l_log_deriv_right for Re s ≥ 11/10.
hf-box-tail: Formalism.HermitianLattices.Ext.BoxTail.tail_contour. Σ_χ is Formalism.ZeroFreeDirichlet.Schi and F_y is Fchi. Perron's formula and the contour shift are tail_shift_identity (perron_formula_character and rectangle_contour_shift_character); the three bounds are tc_right_pt with l_log_deriv_right, tc_horiz_pt with tail_box_negLD, and tc_left_int with tc_log_bound.
hf-pnt-character: QH.psi_thin, proved in the Lean from pt_zero_free (the zero-free region with the exceptional zero excluded), explicitFormula_closed and zerosWindow_closed. ψ(u, χ) − δ_χ u is PI.psi0 χ u. It is a form of the prime number theorem for a primitive character with the classical error term; the published statements give it with an implied constant depending on the excluded region.
hf-chebyshev-integral: QH.g_integral, through l21a. g_χ is QH.G0 χ y, which is Gchi for χ ≠ 1 and the function G of Definition wl-corrected-sums for χ = 1.
hf-norm-primes-short: GlobalTheory.T.normPrimesImagQuad_short_interval_lower_bound, proved in the Lean (GlobalTheory.Hk.normPrimes_short_interval_lower). The primes counted are GlobalTheory.Mem.An.normPrimes d M X (X(1+h)), the primes in (⌊X⌋, ⌊X(1+h)⌋] with NormOne d M. It is a consequence of the prime ideal theorem for the Hecke L-functions of Q(√−d) in the classical zero-free region with Stark's treatment of the exceptional zero; it is not stated in this form in the cited sources.
hf-exceptional-primes: GlobalTheory.choice_count, which is choiceCount_of applied to exceptional_set_count (at most three exceptional primes for each i, exceptional_primes_finite_card_le) and rootsOfUnityCount (at most 2i solutions of x^i = 1 modulo ℓ^w). B_r(g) is Formalism.CyclotomicNorms.BB r g and the condition on ℓ is Exc g i ℓ. The bound for a fixed ℓ is card_mem_BB_fixed_le.
hf-orbit-failure: The probability is exP over the positions other than i₀, as in UpperTheory.BernoulliSumsFrobeniusOrbits.not_good_le, which gives the bound n'C(L₂,K)δ^K + n'(1 − markedLow)^M₀ + n'·binUpper G' δ (N₁ − 1) (Steps 2 to 4, through ngl_windows_le, tail_le, tiles_le and marked_ge; μ is markedLow δ1 r u). Step 5 is orbit_terms with markedLow_bounds (μ ≥ 10^(−(6r+1)) for δ ≤ 1/100). The Lean states the two lemmas separately, with n' in place of the orbit length; the text combines them.
hf-random-selection: UpperTheory.BernoulliSumsFrobeniusOrbits.select. The probability of T is pw p T; the classes are the fibres of a map cl to a finite set; the proof uses the moment identity sel_moment' and sel_exists, which picks a T of positive weight at which a function is at most its mean.
